title: staged-capture-priming-and-kernel-stitching-to-mitigate-warmup-regressions
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: intermittent warmup regressions with fragmented continuous-batching workloads and sparse KV-cache hits were causing spiky latency and rare capture-mismatch fallbacks during CUDA graph replay. This PR introduces a two-part approach: 1) staged capture priming — lightweight, incremental capture probes that prime kernels and the KV cache before committing a long-lived CUDA graph; and 2) kernel stitching — an optimizer that coalesces adjacent small kernels into a single capture-friendly kernel group to reduce capture fragmentation and decrease the number of graph replays. Implementation highlights: added a CapturePrimingCoordinator (runtime/cudagraph/capture_priming.h/.cpp) that runs ephemeral, non-blocking probe captures on a dedicated stream to warm up kernel kernels and populate KV cache entries associated with common prefixes; introduced a compact capture fingerprint (shape+op-hash) to detect safe stitching opportunities; implemented KernelStitcher to emit stitched launch plans when batch fragmentation would otherwise produce many tiny kernels; added a capture epoch counter and conservative fence semantics so probes cannot race with live replays; exposed a runtime flag redwood.cudagraph.priming_enabled and a knob priming_threshold to tune when staged priming triggers; telemetry: new metrics cudagraph.probe_count, cudagraph.stitched_kernels, cudagraph.priming_latency_ms, and cudagraph.replay_fallbacks. Fallbacks: when stitched kernel execution detects an unexpected shape mismatch we fall back to eager execution for that request and schedule a background recapture; capture mismatches are logged with a diagnostic sample id to aid triage. Tests: unit tests for fingerprinting and stitching, integration test that simulates fragmented continuous-batching with varying sequence lengths, and a stress job that ran 48h on staging GPUs. Results: in our internal perf lab, end-to-end p95 generation latency decreased by 6% on mixed-length workloads and cold-start replay fallback rate dropped from 4.2% to 0.3%; memory overhead from priming was <2% on average. Rollout plan: feature-gated off by default for Hosted; enable in Dedicated canaries with default priming_threshold=0.2; monitor cudagraph.replay_fallbacks and priming_latency_ms for 7 days before broad enabling. Related items: ENG-1124 (capture regressions triage), ENG-1199 (continuous batching frag tests).

release_notes: Introduce staged CUDA graph priming and kernel stitching to reduce warmup regressions and decrease p95 latency for fragmented batching workloads; feature-gated and disabled by default for Hosted.
notes: Performance regression mitigation case: reduces rare capture mismatch fallbacks and improves p95 on mixed-length traffic.
Follow-up: add an automated canary that flips priming_enabled and measures cudagraph.replay_fallbacks in production for a week.
Known limitation: stitching is conservative and will not merge kernels across dynamic-shape breakpoints; we plan future work to relax this with typed-shape guards.
